claims.claim: In a recent test, the model helped identify 948 potential issues in the Linux kernel and 81 novel vulnerabilities in the Firefox web browser.
claims.bestSource: OpenAI released a new cybersecurity model. Is that enough?
claims.evidence: Today, the AI giant announced a new model focused on cybersecurity, ChatGPT Cyber, would be made available to the highest tier of users in the cybersecurity program, Daybreak Red, which allows offensive cybersecurity researchers tools for vulnerability hunting and development. Yesterday, OpenAI said that the same model had been used to scan and prepare patches for vulnerabilities in the Linux kernel, finding 948 potential issues. OpenAI also found 81 “novel” vulnerabilities in Firefox, the web browser. It’s unclear if frontier labs are devoting enough of their resources to this issue. Still, OpenAI says just “thousands” of cybersecurity professionals are participating in the Daybreak program, versus a far larger number of potential hackers. OpenAI has insisted that there is a narrow window of time for the people who safeguard digital infrastructure to take action before AI models become even better at hacking and easier to access.
